findings.issue: `id` is set to `https://chorus4ai.org/`, which is also the value of `page`. The dataset identifier and the project landing page are the same URI, so the record asserts that the dataset entity and the website entity are one thing. The bundle supplies no dataset DOI or accession; a more defensible identifier would be a distinct URI (e.g. a fragment on the attested project URL) reserved for the dataset, with `page` retaining the landing page.

`created_by` is `CHoRUS Consortium`. The bundle names 'CHoRUS Consortium' (chorus4ai.org section heading) so the string is attested, but the awarded organization on the NIH RePORTER record is Massachusetts General Hospital and the record elsewhere uses that as `data_governance.accountable_organization`. The value is defensible but weakly anchored; no source states who 'created' the dataset in these terms.

`status` reads 'Partially released under controlled access, with an anticipated final dataset still in preparation'. This is a composed summary sentence rather than a status token; the slot description gives examples of the form draft/published/deprecated. The substance (partial release, controlled access, anticipated final dataset) is already carried in `description`, `updates` and `license_and_use_terms`. Also, the tier-2 source's site-wide banner ('under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives') bears on status and is only recorded in `notes`.

`language: en` is not supported by the bundle. No source states the language of the dataset content. The webinar's eligibility list requires trainees to have a 'Working command of English', which is a statement about program applicants, not about the dataset's content language. Inference from the sources being in English is not evidence about the data.

Several keywords are composed rather than drawn from the bundle. 'intensive care unit' (sources say ICU, PICU, NICU), 'AI-ready dataset' (attested: 'AI-ready data set'), 'multimodal data' and 'medical imaging' (attested: 'Imaging (from PACS)', 'Multimodal & High-Resolution') are paraphrases. This is low-risk restatement, but the list mixes NIH RePORTER 'Preferred terms' with composed terms without distinguishing them.

The list omits `OPEN_MHEALTH`-style precision problems but more importantly includes a single `OTHER` to cover three distinct non-registered standards named in `conforms_to` (EDF+, Persyst, OHNLP schema). One `OTHER` entry for three separate standards under-represents the multivalued slot; either repeat `OTHER` per standard or note the collapse. Additionally, WFDB is described in the source as 'PhysioNet schema extended', so the conformance is to an extension rather than to WFDB as registered — this qualification appears in `conforms_to` prose but is not flagged as a caveat on the enum.

The slot is multivalued and the bundle names six leadership-team members (Eric Rosenthal/MGH, Azra Bihorac/University of Florida, Xiaoqian Jiang/UTHealth Houston, Yulia Strekalova/University of Florida, Parisa Rashidi/University of Florida, Manlik Kwong/Tufts University), each with an explicit affiliation. Only one Creator object is emitted; the other five are named only inside a `source_caveats` prose string. Per the multivalued rule, each distinct attested person with an affiliation should be its own Creator object. Burying five named entities in commentary populates the slot without representing what it declares.

`credit_roles: [project_administration, supervision]` for Eric S. Rosenthal is not supported. The bundle states only that he is 'Principal investigator' on the NIH RePORTER record and appears first on a leadership-team slide. CRediT roles of project administration and supervision are inferred from the PI title, not stated.

`FundingMechanism` declares a `grants` key of range `Grant[]`, and the bundle supplies grant identifiers (project number 1OT2OD032701-01, core project number OT2OD032701, application ID 10472824, award amount 5880300, project start 2022-09-01, project end 2026-11-30). All of this is placed in the free-text `notes` field while the declared structured field `grants` is left empty. Per the class-range rule, evidence answering a declared field should populate that field.

`grantor` reads 'National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund, Bridge2AI program'. This packs the funding agency and the program into one string. The bundle attests 'NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program' and 'funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701'; the composite value is acceptable prose but conflates grantor with program.

`counts: 50000` on the ICU/PICU/NICU admission instance takes the tier-2 figure while the tier-4 webinar states 'over 45K unique admissions' as of August 2025. The disagreement is disclosed in the top-level `source_caveats` but not on the object that carries the disputed number. Per the disagreement rule, the caveat should sit with the value it qualifies (`instances[0].source_caveats`), not only in a distant top-level field.

`counts: 7642` (admissions with radiology data) is in direct tension with the tier-4 webinar's '1000 images available'. The record's top-level caveat correctly notes the units differ, but the instance object itself carries no caveat, and `known_limitations` separately asserts the 1000-image figure as current. A reader of `instances` alone sees 7,642 with no indication of conflict.

`data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37` (Relational Database) is used for both the admission instance and the OMOP row instance. OMOP data are described in the bundle as rows in the OMOP CDM; 37 is a plausible fit for the OMOP row entry, but for 'Patient admission from ICU, PICU, and NICU' the substrate of an admission is not a relational database — the admission is the unit of observation, not the storage form. Per the enum guidance, omit rather than approximate.

`data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:37` (Waveform) is assigned to the EEG waveform instance. B2AI_TOPIC:10 (EKG) is not right either, but the bundle explicitly describes EEG as 'Waveform EEG (hospital database)' and the NIH abstract lists 'Electroencephalography'; B2AI_TOPIC:48 (Neurology) or omission may be more defensible than reusing the telemetry topic. Low confidence either way — flagged as an approximation rather than a clear error.

The `instances` entry for waveform telemetry places '23 Tb of waveform data' in `notes`. The Instance class has no size field, so notes is the residual location, but the same fact is also asserted in `description`. Duplication across description and a structured note is redundant rather than wrong.

`involves_human_subjects: true` is well supported, but the `irb_approval` and `ethics_review_board` fields are absent while `special_populations` carries prose. That is correct given the evidence. However, the record separately asserts in `description` and `instances` a cohort of critically ill hospital patients, and the NIH abstract says data come from 'more than 100,000 critically ill patients' — that figure is the anticipated total, and the record's `description` correctly attributes 100,000 to the anticipated final dataset. No defect in the number; the finding is that `human_subject_research.source_caveats` restates the 100,000 figure in a way that reads as if it describes collected data.

`at_risk_groups_included: true` is inferred, not stated. The bundle states the released admissions come 'from ICU, PICU, and NICU'. That minors are present follows from PICU/NICU, but no source characterizes any group as an at-risk population, and the record's own `source_caveats` concedes the inference. Under prefer-omission, a boolean asserted purely by inference from a ward name is weakly grounded.

`identifiable_elements_present: true` is an inference. The bundle documents de-identification activity in process for imaging, tokenization of notes, and 'approaches that limit re-identification', which implies identifiable source material, but no source states that identifiable elements are present in the released dataset. The asserted boolean is stronger than the evidence.

`privacy_techniques` lists 'A clinical trials processor de-identification component, maintained in the CTP-deid repository'. The bundle shows only a repository named `CTP-deid` in the chorus-ai repository list with no description, no language, and zero stars. Expanding 'CTP' to 'clinical trials processor' is outside-knowledge expansion of an acronym the bundle never expands.

The DeGauss geocoding entry states that geocoding allows 'contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital to be attached to records'. The bundle attests the UF-Geocoding repository ('Open source code to geocode OMOP Location entities via DeGauss') and separately attests, in the NIH abstract, that data elements should 'feature appropriate contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital'. Joining the two into a causal claim ('allowing ... to be attached') is a composed inference not stated by either source. The UF-Geocoding repo is also marked 'Forked from bihorac-LAB/Exposome', which the record does not note.

The `DistributionFormat` class declares `access_urls` and `download_url` (range `uri`), which are left empty across all five entries while the access route is described only in `data_governance`. That placement is correct per the read-the-description rule, so this is not a misplacement — the finding is that no entry carries a `media_type` either, though DICOM and WFDB have conventional media types; those are not stated in the bundle, so omission is right. Net: entries are thin but defensible; noted for completeness only.

`committee_name`, `committee_members` and `committee_contact` are all empty while the access contacts (dbold@emory.edu, jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org) and the program manager (Ciera McCrary, MGH) appear only as email strings inside `access_review_process` and `stewardship_roles` prose. `committee_contact` has range `Person`; Jared Houghtaling is a named person in the bundle (also listed as a Tufts lecturer in the webinar curriculum table). A declared Person-ranged field is left empty while the evidence that answers it sits in free text.

`license_terms` mixes two different objects: the data license (controlled access, signed licensing agreement) and the software license (MIT for the chorus-ai GitHub organization, Apache-2.0 on some repos). The MIT/Apache licenses govern CHoRUS code repositories, not the dataset. Including them in the dataset's license terms risks a reader concluding the data are MIT-licensed. Also `data_use_permission` is unpopulated although the bundle supports at least `ethics_approval_required`-adjacent or `institution_specific` semantics (the '.edu' email requirement) — though no enum value maps cleanly, so omission is arguably correct.

The top-level `license` slot is omitted. This is defensible for the data (controlled access, no named data license), and omitting is better than writing MIT, which governs only the software. Flagged so the omission is recorded as deliberate rather than overlooked.

Both entries invent organization names not present in the bundle: 'CHoRUS consortium Ethics pillar (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)' and 'CHoRUS consortium legal and ethics workstream'. The NIH abstract names a pillar as '2) Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)', but no source calls any body a 'reviewing organization', and 'legal and ethics workstream' appears nowhere. `reviewing_organization` should name an attested reviewing body; the content described (focus groups, community perspectives) is ethics *activity*, not ethics *review*. This may be the wrong slot for this content entirely.

The first `Maintainer` entry omits `role` for the second and third entries while setting `role: academic_institution` on the first. The enum permits `academic_institution`, so the value is valid, but the three entries are inconsistently structured. More substantively, all three place identity information (Ciera McCrary, dbold@emory.edu, jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org) in the free-text `maintainer_details` string; the class offers no Person field, so this is forced — noted as a schema limitation rather than an authoring defect.

Four separate ExternalResource objects each wrap a single string inside the multivalued `external_resources` sub-key, producing a list of objects each containing a one-item list. The nesting is schema-valid but structurally redundant; a single object with four entries, or four objects each with a scalar-shaped entry, would be clearer. Additionally the fourth entry records 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' without a scheme, which will not resolve as written.

The site-wide banner quoted in `notes` reproduces the source's typo 'repoitory' without flagging it, unlike the `maintainers` entry which explicitly flags the 'mgh.havard.edu' typo. Inconsistent treatment of transcription anomalies. Verbatim quotation is correct; the inconsistency is in whether the reader is told.

`timeframe_details` equates the data collection window with the NIH award period (2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30). The award dates are attested, but no source states that retrospective clinical data were *collected from* that period — retrospective extraction during 2022-2026 will cover admissions from earlier years. The record conflates the project period with the clinical data's temporal coverage. The structured `start_date`/`end_date` fields are correctly left empty.

The coverage_limitation entry asserts 'imaging was limited to 1000 images' as a current limitation while `instances` asserts 7,642 admissions with radiology data. The record therefore states two different imaging scales in two places without cross-reference. The top-level `source_caveats` explains the conflict, but a reader consulting `known_limitations` and `instances` separately gets contradictory pictures. The internal inconsistency should be resolved at each site of use.

The representativeness_limitation entry states the 14 hospitals are 'in the United States'. The GitHub organization page lists 'United States of America' as the org location, and eligibility for the training program is US-restricted, but no source states that the 14 data acquisition hospitals are all US-based. Inference from adjacent facts.

Omitted, but the bundle supports at least one entry. The NIH abstract and GitHub README both state that patient-focused efforts 'determine the ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias', and the GitHub README states 'Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort' — implying a recognized representation/sampling bias risk being actively mitigated. A DatasetBias entry with `bias_type: representation_bias` or `sampling_bias` and the attested mitigation is supported.

Omitted. Correct — the bundle documents no patient consent process, and retrospective EHR extraction typically proceeds under waiver. Flagged so the omission is recorded as evidence-driven rather than an oversight.
Omitted. The bundle provides no statement of discouraged or prohibited uses beyond access control. Correct omission, recorded for completeness.

Omitted. Correct — no recommended citation appears in the bundle. However, the chorus4ai.org disclaimer ('This project is funded by the NIH under award number OT2OD032701. The content on this website is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the NIH.') is an acknowledgment statement the bundle supplies and the record does not carry anywhere.

All omitted. `total_size_bytes` could arguably be derived from '23 Tb Waveform data', but that figure covers one modality only, not the whole dataset, and the unit ('Tb' — bits or bytes, decimal or binary) is ambiguous in the source. Omission is correct; recorded so the ambiguity is on file.
All omitted, consistent with the top-level `source_caveats` which states the bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation. Correct and internally consistent.

The holdout test set is described in `splits` as prose but no `DataSubset` is created for it and no fragment identifier is minted, even though `tasks` references external validation against it and `intended_uses` names 'External validation of AI models'. Under the v6 minting rule, a part that another value points at warrants a fragment identifier; here the references are textual rather than structural, so no identifier is strictly required — flagged as a borderline case.

Two ExistingUse objects are emitted, the first containing a single quoted sentence and the second containing two composed examples. The first entry's single quoted string 'Datasets are being used for training activities and publications' is verbatim from the webinar and correct. The second entry's examples are composed summaries of the training program; they are grounded but paraphrased rather than quoted, and the poster/abstract/manuscript entry describes *planned trainee outputs*, not existing uses of the dataset at time of publication.

The clinical-notes entry sets `was_inferred_derived: true`. Tokenization is a transformation of directly-observed clinical documentation rather than inference or derivation of new facts; `was_directly_observed: true` with the tokenization noted in `acquisition_details` (or in `preprocessing_strategies`, where it already appears) would be more accurate. The boolean overstates the epistemic distance.

The description states 'more than 60 consortium members'. The source reads '60+ CHoRUS consortium members across 20 different institutions'. Faithful. However the description also states data are 'contributed by 14 data acquisition hospitals within a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers' — chorus4ai.org says '14 Data contributing hospitals' and GitHub says '20 academic centers, of which 14 will contribute as Data Acquisition centers' (future tense). The record renders a future-tense GitHub claim as present-tense fact.

The value is a long paragraph fusing two distinct access routes: the general CHoRUS request route (email dbold@emory.edu / jared.houghtaling@tuftsmedicine.org) and the AIM-AHEAD training-program route (registration form, licensing agreement, .edu email, compute provisioning). These are different processes for different populations; merging them into one prose block obscures that a general researcher does not go through the training-program registration form.

summary: Audited the full CHoRUS record against the four-file declared bundle (NIH RePORTER project page, AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 webinar, chorus4ai.org project documentation, chorus-ai GitHub overview). The record is broadly well-grounded and its top-level source_caveats correctly identifies the central tier-2/tier-4 disagreement over admission and imaging counts. Principal defects: (1) creators collapses six attested, individually-affiliated leadership-team members into one Creator object with the other five relegated to prose commentary, violating the multivalued-entity rule; (2) funders leaves the declared grants: Grant[] field empty while placing every grant identifier, amount and date into free-text notes; (3) data_governance leaves committee_contact (range Person), committee_members and committee_name empty while the named access contacts sit inside prose strings; (4) ethical_reviews invents two reviewing_organization names ('Ethics pillar', 'legal and ethics workstream') that no source states, and arguably records ethics activity in a slot meant for ethics review; (5) the imaging figures (7,642 admissions in instances vs 1000 images in known_limitations) contradict each other at their points of use, with the reconciling caveat located only at top level, and the same applies to the 50,000-vs-45K admission count; (6) id duplicates page, giving the dataset and the website one identity. Unsupported or over-strong values: language: en, at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included, is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present, creators.credit_roles, 'clinical trials processor' as an expansion of CTP-deid, 'in the United States' for the 14 hospitals, the DeGauss-to-distance-to-hospital causal join, and the equation of the NIH award period with the clinical data's temporal coverage. Shape issues: a single OTHER covering three distinct standards; B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37 approximated onto a patient-admission instance; status carrying a composed sentence rather than a status token; external_resources nesting four single-item lists; license_and_use_terms mixing the MIT/Apache software licenses with the controlled-access data terms. Supported omission: known_biases, for which the bundle attests both a representation/sampling bias concern and its federated-sampling mitigation. Correctly-omitted slots (license, doi, version, issued, citation, file_collections, collection_consents, discouraged_uses) are consistent with the record's own stated caveats.
